01-hook: You get your best ideas in the shower. Driving. Walking the dog. And every single one of them vanishes before you sit down. What if your phone could capture them in ten seconds flat?
02-intro: I'm Jason from PatchMyDay and today we're building this — a single iPhone Shortcut called Brain Dump. You tap it, talk for as long as you want, and it saves a timestamped markdown file straight to iCloud. No app install. No subscription. Just Shortcuts, which is already on your phone. Let's build it from scratch in under six minutes.
03-dictate-text: Alright, new shortcut. Tap the plus. First thing we need is input — your voice. Search for 'Dictate Text' and add it. This is the action that fires up the mic and transcribes whatever you say in real time. Under 'Stop Listening,' set it to 'After Pause.' That means it'll keep recording until you stop talking — no arbitrary cutoff. Could be five seconds, could be five minutes. Doesn't matter. It waits for you. Go ahead and rename this shortcut 'Brain Dump' at the top. Give it a brain emoji if you're feeling fancy. Now we have raw text. But raw text with no timestamp is just chaos. Let's fix that.
04-timestamp: Next action — 'Current Date.' This grabs the exact moment you run the shortcut. But the default format is ugly and useless for filenames. So right below it, add 'Format Date.' Tap into it, switch from 'Short' to 'Custom,' and type this exact string: lowercase y-y-y-y, dash, uppercase M-M, dash, lowercase d-d, dash, uppercase H-H-lowercase m-m. That gives you year-month-day-hour-minute. Clean. Sortable. Obsidian-friendly. This formatted string is about to become your filename, so get it right. If you see something like '2026-04-10-1231' in the preview — you're golden.
05-save-file: Now we assemble the actual file. Add a 'Text' action. Tap inside the text block, and from the variables bar, grab 'Dictated Text' — that blue pill from Step 1. That's it. That's your file body. Everything you said, transcribed, sitting in a text block. Now add 'Save File.' This is where it lands. Set the destination to iCloud Drive. I like to put mine in a folder called 'journal underscore inbox' — think of it as a landing zone. Your raw brain dumps pile up here until you process them. If the folder doesn't exist yet, don't worry — Shortcuts will create it the first time you run this. Make sure 'Ask Where to Save' is toggled OFF. You want zero friction. Tap, talk, done.
06-rename-notify: Almost done. Now we need a real filename — because 'Text.txt' tells you nothing six months from now. Add a 'Rename' action. Set the input to Saved File, and for the new name, tap in, grab your 'Formatted Date' variable from earlier, then type dash-brain-dump-dot-m-d after it. So you end up with something like '2026-04-10-1231-brain-dump.md.' Beautiful. Markdown extension means it plays nice with Obsidian, Notion imports, any plain text editor. Last action: 'Show Notification.' Title it 'Brain Dump Saved.' In the body, drop the same Formatted Date variable so you get a little confirmation ping that says exactly which file just got created. This is your dopamine hit — the proof it worked. Six actions total. That's the whole shortcut.
07-demo: Let's run it. Tap Brain Dump. Mic's hot — talk. 'Idea for the PatchMyDay channel — do a video on building AI agents that process journal entries and extract action items.' I stop talking. It stops listening. Bam — notification. 'Brain Dump Saved.' Now let's verify. Open Files. iCloud Drive, Shortcuts, journal underscore inbox. There it is. 2026-04-10-1231-brain-dump.md. Tap it open — and there's my exact transcription. Sitting in iCloud. Already synced to my Mac. Already visible in Obsidian because I've got that folder in my vault. Ten seconds from thought to saved file. The whole point is you never open an app, never type a character, never think about where to put it. You just talk.
08-power-tips: Three power moves. One — long press the shortcut tile, 'Add to Home Screen.' Now it's a one-tap app icon on your dock. I keep mine right next to the camera. Two — this works with Siri. Just say 'Hey Siri, Brain Dump' and it fires hands-free. Perfect for driving. You never touch the phone. Three — and this is where it gets interesting — that journal underscore inbox folder is just a directory on iCloud. Which means you can point a script at it. A Python script. An AI agent. A cron job that runs every night, reads your dumps, extracts action items, and drops a summary into your task manager. That's not hypothetical — that's what I'm building next. We're turning shower thoughts into structured workflows.
09-cta: That's it. Seven actions. Zero dollars. Your ideas stop disappearing. If this was useful — subscribe. I'm Jason, I'm a WAF engineer by day, and this channel is where cybersecurity meets AI automation meets not losing your best ideas to the void. Next video — I'm building the AI agent that actually reads these brain dumps, pulls out the action items, and files them into a task board automatically. It's half done and it's kind of terrifying how well it works. Hit subscribe so you don't miss it. I'll see you in that one.
